newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sidek trading suspension lifted - Bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Sidek trading suspension lifted - Bolsa.

text.p: Trading in shares listed by debt-ridden conglomerate Grupo Sidek reopened on Monday after a suspension lasting three business days, the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) said on Monday.
"The BMV has lifted the suspension to allow trading in shares listed by Grupo Sidek as of March 31," a BMV statement said.
Sidek shares will remain subject to possible suspension as long as the company is not able to confirm that it is listed on an international stock exchange, the BMV added.
The New York Stock Exchange indefinitely suspended Sidek shares on March 20. Sidek has since said it intends to issue over the counter shares in New York.
Sidek, whose principal subsidiaries are steelmakers Simec and tourism firm Situr, has had severe debt problems since a shock devaluation of the peso in December 1994.
